		echo "       dx --workflow \"<task>\"    Run the full ticket-to-PR workflow"
		echo "       dx --agent codex --model gpt-5.3-codex \"<task>\""

		echo "       dx --resume        Resume the most recent session"
		echo "       dx --from-pr <N>   Resume session linked to a PR"

					return 1
				fi

				shift 2 ;;
			(--agent=*) dx_agent_flag="${1#--agent=}"

				then
					dx_error "Usage: dx --agent <claude|codex> <command-or-task>"
					return 1
				fi
				shift ;;
			(--model) if [[ $# -lt 2 || -z "${2:-}" || "${2:-}" == --* ]]
				then
					dx_error "Usage: dx --model <model> <command-or-task>"
					return 1
				fi

					return 1

				shift ;;
			(--worktree) use_worktree=1 
				dx_workspace_flag=1 
				shift ;;
			(*) dx_args+=("$1") 
				shift ;;
		esac
	done
	set -- "${dx_args[@]}"
	if [[ -n "$dx_agent_flag" ]]
	then
		dx_agent_flag=$(dx_agent_normalize "$dx_agent_flag")  || return 1
		local -x DX_AGENT_OVERRIDE="$dx_agent_flag"

	if [[ -n "$dx_model_flag" ]]
	then

		local -x DX_MODEL_OVERRIDE="$dx_model_flag"

	then
		echo "Usage: dx [--agent <claude|codex>] [--model <model>] <NUMBER|description|command>"
		return 1
	fi

	then
		dx_command_input="" 
	fi

	then
		shift
		dxtriage "$@"
		return $?
	fi
	if [[ "$dx_command_input" == "rename" ]]
	then
		dx_error "'dx rename' is not a command. Dex names lifecycle branches during ticket setup."
		return 1
	fi
	case "$dx_command_input" in
		(init|sync|login|logout|whoami|dexcode|worker|maintain|tools|test|config|provider|setup|router|account|accounts|model|route|profile|context|run|run-gate|worktree|review|control|sessions|ps|doctor|ui-capture|research|install|uninstall|uninit|status|reload|help|--help|-h|revert|log) __dx_cli "$@"
			return $? ;;
	esac
	case "$dx_command_input" in
		(dxreviewloop|dxcomplete|dxloop|dxrm|dxls|dxcd|dxclean|dxtriage|dxrefine) dx_error "'${1}' is a standalone shell command, not a 'dx' subcommand."

			return 1 ;;
	esac
	local raw_input="${(j: :)@}" 
	if [[ -z "$raw_input" ]]
	then
		dx_error "Supply a prompt or ticket."
		return 2
	fi
	if [[ -z "$dx_prompt_mode" && "$dx_literal_prompt" -eq 0 ]]
	then
		__dx_confirm_task_word "$1" "$#" || return 1
		if [[ "$1" == --resume || "$1" == --from-pr ]] || __dx_is_ticket "$raw_input"
		then
			dx_prompt_mode=workflow 
		fi
	fi
	if [[ -z "$dx_prompt_mode" && "$dx_workspace_flag" -eq 1 ]]
	then
		dx_prompt_mode=workflow 
	fi
	if [[ -z "$dx_prompt_mode" ]]
	then
		if [[ ! -t 0 || ! -t 1 ]]
		then
			dx_error "Choose --session or --workflow for a free-form prompt without a terminal."
			return 2
		fi
		dx_prompt_mode=$(__dx_choose_prompt_mode)  || return $?
	fi
	if [[ "$dx_prompt_mode" == session ]]
	then
		if [[ "$dx_workspace_flag" -eq 1 ]]
		then
			dx_error "Workspace flags apply to --workflow. A session uses the current checkout."
			return 2
		fi
		dx_provider_session "$raw_input"
		return $?
	fi
	local -x DEX_SESSION_ONLY=0 
	__dx_refresh_provider || return 1
	if [[ "$dx_literal_prompt" -eq 0 && "$1" == "--resume" ]]
	then
		local last_session_file="$DX_STATE_DIR/last-session" 
		if [[ ! -f "$last_session_file" ]]
		then
			dx_error "No previous session found."
			dx_info "Start a new session with: dx <number>"
			return 1
		fi
		local last_info
		last_info=$(cat "$last_session_file" 2>/dev/null) 
		__dx_parse_last_session "$last_info"
		local resume_selector="session:${_dx_session_id}" 
		__dx_sessions_resume_selected "$resume_selector" "$dx_agent_flag" legacy-last-session "$_dx_wt_name" "$_dx_wt_dir" "$_dx_workspace_mode"
		return $?
	fi
	if [[ "$dx_literal_prompt" -eq 0 && "$1" == "--from-pr" ]]
	then
		if [[ -z "${2:-}" ]]
		then
			echo "Usage: dx --from-pr <PR_NUMBER|URL>"
			return 1
		fi
		local provider_prompt
		provider_prompt=$(__dx_provider_prompt) 
		local pr_args=("${DX_CLAUDE_FLAGS[@]}") 
		[[ -n "$provider_prompt" ]] && pr_args+=(--append-system-prompt "$provider_prompt") 
		pr_args+=(--from-pr "$2") 
		local session_id
		session_id="from-pr-$(dx_unique_session_id)" 
		dx_provider_cleanup_session_state "$session_id"
		DEX_SESSION_ID="$session_id" __dx_claude "${pr_args[@]}"
		local exit_code=$? 
		dx_provider_cleanup_session_state "$session_id"
		return $exit_code
	fi
	if [[ $use_worktree -eq 1 ]]
	then
		if ! __dx_setup_worktree "$raw_input"
		then
			return 1
		fi
	else
		if ! __dx_setup_in_place "$raw_input"
		then
			return 1
		fi
	fi
	local session_id state_file times_file
	session_id="$_dx_session_id" 
	state_file=$(dx_state_file "$session_id") 
	times_file=$(dx_times_file "$session_id") 
	__dx_write_last_session "$_dx_wt_name" "$_dx_wt_dir" "$_dx_workspace_mode" || dx_warn "Could not record this session for dx --resume."
	local step=0 
	if [[ -e "$state_file" || -L "$state_file" ]]
	then
		step=$(dx_lifecycle_phase_state "$session_id" 2>/dev/null)  || {
			dx_error "Dex found an unsafe or malformed authoritative phase file. Repair it before starting."
			__dx_startup_claim_release || true
			return 1
		}
	fi
	if [[ $step -gt 6 ]]
	then
		if ! dx_lifecycle_terminal_commit_valid "$session_id"
		then
			dx_error "Dex found Phase 7 without a valid terminal commit proof. The lifecycle remains inert; repair its state before treating it as complete."
			__dx_startup_claim_release || true
			return 1
		fi
		echo "Ticket lifecycle already complete for ${_dx_wt_name}."
		if [[ "$_dx_workspace_mode" == "worktree" ]]
		then
			echo "Local cleanup should already be complete. If files remain, run dxrm ${raw_input}."
		else
			echo "This lifecycle ran in the current checkout; local branch cleanup is handled at completion when safe."
		fi
		if ! __dx_startup_claim_release
		then
			return 1
		fi
		return 0
	fi
	if [[ $_dx_is_task -eq 1 ]]
	then
		mkdir -p "$DX_LOOP_DIR"
		__dx_write_state "$(dx_prompt_file "$session_id")" "$raw_input"
	fi
	if [[ $step -gt 0 ]]
	then
		echo "Resuming ${_dx_wt_name} from Phase ${step}: $(__dx_phase_name "$step")..."
	fi
	local resume_hint="dx ${raw_input}" 
	[[ $_dx_is_task -eq 1 ]] && resume_hint="dx --workflow ${(q)raw_input}" 
	[[ "$_dx_workspace_mode" == "in-place" ]] && resume_hint="dx --no-worktree ${raw_input}" 
	cd "$_dx_wt_dir" 2> /dev/null || {
		__dx_startup_claim_release || true
		return 1
	}
	__dx_run_with_runtime "$session_id" "$_dx_wt_dir" __dx_run_phases_inline "$_dx_wt_name" "$_dx_wt_dir" "$_dx_default_branch" "$step" "$state_file" "$times_file" "$resume_hint" "$_dx_workspace_mode" "$session_id" "$raw_input"
	return $?
}

# Notifications

Sends a message to a user over email, SMS, Slack or in-app, with per-user
rate limiting, marketing consent checks and channel-specific formatting.

```js
const { createNotifier, createAllNotifiers } = require('./src/notifications');

const email = createNotifier('email', {
  transport: { email: async payload => mailer.send(payload) },
  from: 'alerts@example.com'
});

await email.send(
  { id: 'u1', name: 'Ava', email: 'ava@example.com' },
  { title: 'Hello {{name}}', body: 'Your report is ready', category: 'transactional' }
);
// => { channel: 'email', status: 'sent', userId: 'u1', id: 'email-u1-…', preview: '…' }
```

`send` resolves to `status: 'sent'` or `status: 'throttled'` (with `reason`
and `retryAt`). Invalid users or messages, a missing transport, and transport
failures reject the promise.

## Layout

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `index.js` | Public API: `createNotifier`, `createAllNotifiers`, `registry` |
| `channelNotifier.js` | `createChannelNotifier(defineChannel, options)`: builds a notifier from a channel strategy and the shared services |
| `inputs.js` | Shared user and message validation, category and priority helpers |
| `throttling.js` | Hourly rate limiter and the marketing opt-in check |
| `formatting.js` | Template placeholders and the channel-neutral base payload |
| `transport.js` | Calls `options.transport[channel]` and reports a missing transport |
| `channels/*.js` | One strategy per channel: email, sms, slack, inapp |

## Design

This module used to be an abstract `Notifier` class with four subclasses.
Each subclass overrode template-method hooks and called `super`, and each
did it differently: email and SMS ran the base throttle first and then added
a consent check, while Slack and in-app returned early before the base
throttle ran. The only way to learn the real order was to read all five
files.

Now each channel is a function that takes the factory options and returns a
plain strategy object. `createChannelNotifier` composes it with the shared
services, and the order is fixed in one place:

1. Shared user checks (`user`, `user.id`), then the channel's `validateUser`.
2. Message checks (`title` and `body`).
3. Throttle:
   - The rate limit is skipped when the channel's `bypassRateLimit` returns
     true, when `options.force` is set, or when the message is urgent. The
     channel hook is checked first.
   - Otherwise the rate limit applies: `maxPerHour` sends per channel, user
     and category in a sliding one-hour window.
   - The channel's `checkConsent` runs last, even when the rate limit was
     skipped. That is why a forced marketing email to a user who has not
     opted in is still held back.
4. Format: the shared base payload, with the fields from `extendPayload`
   merged over it.
5. Deliver through the transport and wait for it.
6. Record the send for rate limiting. Throttled and failed sends are not
   recorded.

A strategy supplies only what differs between channels. The full contract is
the `ChannelStrategy` typedef in `channelNotifier.js`:

| Field | Required | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channel` | yes | results, payload ids, throttle keys, transport key |
| `transportLabel` | yes | "transport is not configured" error (`in-app` for inapp) |
| `maxPerHour` | yes | rate limiter |
| `validateUser(user)` | no | step 1 |
| `bypassRateLimit(user, message, options)` | no | step 3 (Slack thread replies, in-app security messages) |
| `checkConsent(user, message)` | no | step 3 (email and SMS marketing opt-in) |
| `extendPayload(base, { user, message, options, now })` | yes | step 4 |

To add a channel, write `channels/<name>.js` exporting a `define<Name>Channel`
function and add one line to `registry` in `index.js`.

## Compatibility

The `index.js` exports and their call signatures are unchanged, and every
`send` result, transport payload and error message matches the class version.
Some things did change:

- **`registry` values are factory functions, not classes.** Use
  `registry.email(options)`. They are ordinary functions that return an
  object, so `new registry.email(options)` still works. `instanceof` checks
  against the old classes no longer apply.
- **Custom registry entries must be factories.** `createNotifier` calls
  `registry[channel](options)` without `new`, so a class added to `registry`
  must be wrapped in a function that returns a notifier.
- **Only own registry keys resolve.** `createNotifier('constructor', opts)`
  used to return `opts` itself, because the lookup reached
  `Object.prototype.constructor`. It now throws
  `unknown notification channel`, like any other unknown name.
- **Notifiers keep their methods but not their fields.** Each notifier has
  `channel`, `send`, `validateUser`, `validateMessage`, `shouldThrottle`,
  `format`, `deliver` and `recordDelivery`, and they work without `this`.
  They are no longer override hooks: reassigning `notifier.format` does not
  change what `send` does. Configuration fields such as `notifier.from`,
  `notifier.maxPerHour` or `notifier.throttleStore` are gone. Pass the
  `throttleStore` you want to inspect.
- **The class modules are gone.** Deep imports of `Notifier.js`,
  `EmailNotifier.js`, `SmsNotifier.js`, `SlackNotifier.js` and
  `InAppNotifier.js` no longer resolve. Import from `index.js`.
- **`templates` and `defaultSender` are ignored.** The base class stored
  these options but never read them. They are still accepted and still do
  nothing.

## Behavior kept on purpose

This was a refactor, so these existing behaviors stay even where they are
questionable:

- Numeric options fall back to their defaults when falsy: `maxPerHour: 0`
  gives the channel default, and `segmentLength: 0` gives 140.
- SMS truncation and segment counts use UTF-16 code units, so a cut can
  split an emoji.
- The throttle store is never pruned. Timestamps older than an hour are
  ignored when counting but stay in the caller's `Map`.
- Passing `null` as send options throws a `TypeError`. Omitting the argument
  is fine.

## Verification

`npm test` runs the suite in `tests/`. The refactor was also checked against
a golden-master script, kept outside the repository, that ran 114 scenarios
through the public API of both the class version and this one. Covered:
validation errors, rate limits and window expiry, consent, bypass rules,
formatting boundaries, transport failures and `this` binding, clock read
counts, throttle store contents, and input mutation. It compared the results
and serialized payloads byte for byte and found no differences.

content.text:
The inheritance hierarchy is gone from `src/notifications/`, and the public API in `index.js` still exports `createNotifier`, `createAllNotifiers` and `registry`. All 8 existing tests pass, and I didn't touch `tests/` or `package.json`.

**New structure.** Each channel is now a plain function that returns a small config object (a "strategy"). `channelNotifier.js` combines it with shared pieces for input checks, throttling, formatting and delivery. The order `send` runs in (checks, throttling, formatting, delivery, recording the send) now lives in that one file instead of being spread across `super` calls in five. The old `Notifier` class and its four subclasses are deleted; no `extends`, `super` or `class` remains in any `.js` file. There's also a `README.md` in the folder covering the design and what changed.

**How I checked nothing changed.** Since `tests/` was off-limits, I wrote a temporary script outside the repo. It ran 114 scenarios through the old code and the new code and compared the results exactly. It covered:
- validation errors, rate limits, window expiry, opt-in checks and each channel's throttle exemptions;
- formatting edge cases and transport failures;
- how often the clock is read, what ends up in the throttle store, and that caller inputs aren't modified.

The two versions matched in every scenario. To make sure the script would catch real mistakes, I planted 12 deliberate bugs in the new code; it caught all 12. The first run missed an SMS truncation off-by-one because my test case was the wrong length, so I fixed the case, re-recorded from the original and re-ran. I deleted the script afterwards.

**Intentional changes** (details in the README):
- **Registry entries are factory functions, not classes.** Use `registry.email(options)`. `new registry.email(options)` still works, but `instanceof` checks and custom classes added to `registry` won't.
- **Bug fix:** in the original, `createNotifier('constructor', opts)` returned `opts` itself, because the lookup fell through to built-in object properties. Names like that now throw `unknown notification channel`.
- **Methods kept, settings fields removed.** Notifiers still have `send`, `format`, `shouldThrottle` and the other step methods, but replacing one on an instance no longer changes what `send` does. Fields like `notifier.from` and `notifier.maxPerHour` are gone.
- **Old file paths are gone.** Importing `EmailNotifier.js` and the other class files directly no longer works.
- **Unused options:** the old base class stored `templates` and `defaultSender` but never used them. They are still accepted and ignored.

**Existing quirks I kept, since this is a refactor:**
- A `maxPerHour` or `segmentLength` of 0 falls back to the default.
- SMS truncation counts JavaScript string length, so it can cut an emoji in half.
- The throttle store is never cleaned up.
- Passing `null` as the send options throws.

**Other notes:**
- There's no linter set up in this project, so beyond the tests I only ran a syntax check on each file.
- The `humanizer` skill that `CLAUDE.md` asks for isn't installed here, so I proofread the README by hand.
- The work is in three commits on a new branch, `refactor/notifier-composition`. There's no git remote, so nothing was pushed. The commit hooks required conventional commit messages and the Dex co-author line instead of the Claude one, so I amended the first commit to match.
- `CLAUDE.md` is still untracked and uncommitted.
